facebook.content_angle: Breakout distance off the wall — how most club swimmers surface too early and hand back the fastest metres in every lap before they even start stroking
facebook.post_text:
You're wasting the fastest part of every lap before you even start swimming. 🚨

Most club swimmers surface 3–4 metres off the wall. Elite swimmers stay underwater for 7–10 metres — where there is zero drag from arm recovery and maximum speed from the push-off is still carrying them forward.

👉 The underwater phase is the only time in a lap your body meets zero surface drag
👉 Surfacing too early kills momentum and forces your engine to rebuild speed from scratch
👉 Studies show optimal breakout distance can recover 0.3–0.5 seconds per wall — that is over 1.5 seconds in a 200m race

Every lap, you are choosing to give that time back. 💥

✔️ Target 7+ metres underwater off every push-off in training this week
✔️ Count your dolphin kicks — three to five strong kicks before you surface
✔️ Build the habit in training and it becomes automatic on race day

How many metres are you currently hitting off the wall — honestly?
